strengths: One clock writer: every road (Edit campaign, setPhase, the advance, the rewind, the Eclipse, the season reset, a console) ends in setClock, whose read-modify-write is one step of serialWrite(CLOCK_KEY), and every rule of the edge - no trial opened in an Eclipse, no Eclipse begun in a trial, the stopwatch's stamps, the day boards' marks - is decided once there (scripts/clock.mjs:135-290).

The boundary is given once and can be taken back for five minutes: refilledFor names the boundary, lastAdvance keeps the budgets, search tokens and seals in a GM store rather than the world clock (after 72-canary found actor ids there), and the memory chains four deep (scripts/clock.mjs:381-430, 507-668).

The phase owns its state: every road out of the trial closes the floor, the vote, the voices, the sentence and the bodies, and every road in opens the budget, the reset, the mute and the Key fee, in an order each step explains (scripts/clock.mjs:999-1140).
A private card with no reader is dropped, never published, and a veiled card with none is dropped too (scripts/utils.mjs:815-836).
A failure log that keeps the newest 60, counts repeats on their own row and counts what it dropped, testable on a log of its own (scripts/utils.mjs:279-331).
primaryGmId prefers a full Gamemaster, counts an arriving GM and a leaving one, and takes the user list from a test (scripts/utils.mjs:485-496).

plural, listOf and localeFormat read the page's language, not the live setting or the browser's locale, with Polish's negated list written by hand where Intl has none (scripts/utils.mjs:55-105, 565-584).

The Event panel draws text with textContent only, so no card can carry markup; a spectator gets no incident card at all; and the motive card a bystander sees is the countdown the incident's first private move found (scripts/events.mjs:98-123, 192-243, 827-894).
steps.mjs: one runner whose record is saved after every step, a save that fails fails its step and stops the rest, and a Finish runs only what is not done (scripts/steps.mjs:59-121).

Breakdown and Wounded are applied only on the primary, one pass at a time per actor, chained so the newer values win; the state sounds are decided on each browser from the same write (scripts/states.mjs:89-98, 337-390).
Daggerheart's automation values are kept before the module switches them off and can be given back (scripts/states.mjs:163-237).
Timed effects are a GM store with an owner's copy sent addressed and only to that owner, received only for characters this user owns (scripts/timed-effects.mjs:258-336).

The item draw is one list of named steps over a context the suite can hand in (rng, tables, trail), and each step says what it drew (category, tier, goal) rather than what was asked (scripts/tables-pools.mjs:840-1003).

Table names are kept with their whole history, English and Polish, so a world installed in any language under any older wording is still found, and refreshTableCopy renames only names this module gave in English (scripts/tables-pools.mjs:75-117, 253-313).

The Item tables window writes only fields that changed, refuses an emptied name at the field with the reason beside it, and writes what is on screen before a table switch takes it away (scripts/tables-editor.mjs:519-540, 1407-1500).

findings.title: A Next time of day pressed while an incident runs before Stage 6 refills every bystander's actions and restocks the search tokens on their screens, while their clock stays frozen
findings.where: scripts/clock.mjs:784-857 (applyTimeOfDayChange: resetAllActions and SearchTokens.reset on every move, whoever is told), 881-917 (only the card is narrowed); scripts/boundary.mjs:134-145 (nextTimeOfDay: resetActions true) and 455-462 (no round, so nothing stops the move); scripts/actions.mjs:468-479, 416-462
findings.what_happens: The clock moves in private during an incident before Stage 6 (Dawid, 26.08): the time-of-day card is whispered to the GMs and the incident's audience, the HUD of a bystander keeps the clock from before the incident (hud-elapsed.mjs clockForDisplay) and, since E17 fix p2-G3, even the motive card keeps its old countdown, because 'the card turned Due on every bystander's screen at the move inside the incident'. But the move itself is made by the same applyTimeOfDayChange as any other: the GM panel's Next time of day (the one ordinary road with no Eclipse, which an incident does not refuse: askReadiness opens no round in an incident and answers go) passes resetActions: true, so resetAllActions writes every living character's actions back to its budget, the bystanders' included, and SearchTokens.reset refills every room. Both are world writes every browser draws at once (the sheet's action row, the room's pips). The comment at 889-890 says so ('Everything else the change did - refills, restocks - happened either way; only who is TOLD changes') but the refill is a tell of the same kind as the motive card E17 fixed.
findings.failure_scenario: A killer and victim fight in the boiler room in the afternoon; the GM presses Next time of day to put the fight into the evening; a student who spent both actions before the incident sees their sheet go back to 2 / 2 and their room's search pips refill while their HUD still reads Afternoon, and knows the GM has moved the hour for somebody.
findings.expected: What a bystander's screen shows of an hour moved inside the incident is what the HUD shows: nothing (scripts/clock.mjs:881-890, hud-elapsed.mjs:176-187), as the motive card was held to (events.mjs:91-97).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a guard on the road: nextTimeOfDay refuses only during an Eclipse (boundary.mjs:136-139); roundAllowed bars a round's go, but with an incident already running askReadiness opens no round and answers go at once (boundary.mjs:315-322, 461); startRefusal refuses the Eclipse road in an incident, not this one. resetActionsFor skips only a Monokuma and the published dead (actions.mjs:421-437), not a bystander; resetAllActions has no incident test. The refill and the restock are world writes (an actor's system.resources and flags; the searchTokens setting), drawn by every browser. The sheet's action row and the HUD's pips do not read clockForDisplay (grep: clockForDisplay is read by boundary, clock, day-summary, eclipse, explain, hud-elapsed, hud, incident-store and murder-rules only). Not refuted. Whether a GM moves the hour mid-incident often enough to matter is the table's; the module offers it.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 E17-T10 (named in events.mjs:95-97 and hud-elapsed.mjs:164) holds the motive card and the HUD for a bystander; no test names a bystander's action budget or search pips across a private move (grep of tests-tier2.mjs for 'bystander' with refill or restock: none). Result not read.

l1.what: Whether a bystander's own screen changes when the GM moves the hour inside an incident before Stage 6
recipe: 1. GM and three players; P3's character spends both actions in Daily Life.
2. Open a direct murder between P1's and P2's characters and let the opening succeed (stage incident).
3. GM: panel, Next time of day.
4. On P3's page read the sheet's action row, the HUD's time of day and the room tile's search pips before and after.
l1.settles_if: P3's actions go back to 2 / 2 or the pips refill while the HUD keeps the old hour: the finding stands. Nothing on P3's page changes until the incident ends: refuted.

findings.title: A timed effect whose take-back throws is dropped all the same, its bonus left on the sheet for good, and the throw stops every other row's end at that boundary
findings.where: scripts/timed-effects.mjs:201-212 (endTimedEffect: take in try, the row dropped in finally, no catch), 222-228 (endTimedEffects), 354-367 (endAtEclipseStart: keepEndedAtStart only after the loop), 396-404 (the hooks catch and log)
findings.what_happens: endTimedEffect runs the kind's take (a trustedWrite of the trait back down, or of the Experience's deletion) inside try, and writes the list without the row in finally. A take that throws therefore still drops the row: the +n on the trait, or the Experience, stays on the sheet and no row is left to end it, on any later boundary. The throw is not caught there, so it leaves endTimedEffects or endAtEclipseStart mid-loop: every row after it, of every character, is not ended at this boundary (it waits for the next time of day), and at an Eclipse's start keepEndedAtStart is never reached, so the rows already ended are not kept for the Eclipse's take-back either. The hooks at 398-404 log the throw to the GM's console alone.
findings.failure_scenario: Two students hold a +2 Body from the gym until the time of day ends; at the Eclipse the first one's write fails (a sheet write refused or the connection drops), so that student keeps +2 Body for the rest of the season with nothing listed on the sheet, and the second keeps theirs through the dark as well.
findings.expected: A row is dropped only once what it did is taken back, or is kept and said to the GMs; one row's failure does not hold the others (the module's own runner keeps each step in its own try, steps.mjs:81-94).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a catch around the call: endTimedEffects and endAtEclipseStart call it bare in their loops; registerTimedEffects catches only the whole promise (398-404). take can throw: trustedWrite is an actor update through resource-guard.mjs, awaited with no catch in KINDS (54-61, 79-84). putBackAtTakeBack catches per row (388-390), the end does not. The headless measurement at 20-22 is of a GM's own edit, not of a failed write. How often a primary GM's actor update throws at a table is not measured.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 rows naming endTimedEffect (11 mentions in tests-tier2.mjs) drive successful ends; none plants a take that throws. Result not read.

findings.title: Renaming a room's table in Item tables repoints the rooms but leaves its split tables ('<old> - Tier N', '<old> - Murder Weapons') on the old name, where no draw reads them
findings.where: scripts/tables-editor.mjs:1203-1213 (repointRooms: the rooms' flag only), 1225-1248 (Rename); scripts/tables-pools.mjs:752-754 (roomTableNames), 768-775 (isRoomTableOf), 893-933 (the room's draws read `${base} - ...`)
findings.what_happens: A room stores the name of its table (drpgItemTable), and the draw reads the room's tables as that base and its suffixes: '<base> - Tier N', '<base> - <plural>', '<base>' (drawRoomNamed), and every table '<base> - <suffix>' for drawRoomAny. Since 1.2.115 a Rename of the flat table repoints every room that named it to the new name, so the room's base changes - but the split tables keep the old base in their names, and nothing renames them or says they were left. From then on drawRoomNamed asks for '<new> - Tier N' and '<new> - Murder Weapons', which do not exist, and isRoomTableOf no longer counts the old split tables as the room's: the room draws from its flat table alone, or from the world's pools when that is empty. The split tables still show on the Room pools tab (their roomPool flag), so the window looks as before.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM who stocked 'Kitchen', 'Kitchen - Tier 2' and 'Kitchen - Murder Weapons' renames 'Kitchen' to 'Cafeteria' in Item tables; every Search for a weapon in the kitchen now draws from the flat table's snacks, while the window still lists both split tables full of knives.
findings.expected: The split tables follow their base (or the Rename names the tables it left), as the rooms were made to follow it in 1.2.115 (tables-editor.mjs:1194-1202).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a second step after repointRooms: wirePaneHeading's Rename calls current().update({ name }) and repointRooms only (1237-1238); poolNameRefusal checks the new name, not its family (402-422). Checked that the split tables are a room's by name alone: drawRoomNamed uses ctx.tables.getName on the built names (895-896), drawRoomAny filters by isRoomTableOf(ctx.roomBase, ...) (924); neither reads a flag linking a split table to its room. A room that names a split table directly (not its base) is untouched, as expected. Not refuted.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 'a room table renamed in the Item tables window keeps the rooms that draw from it' (scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:67927) renames a flat table with no split tables. Result not read.

findings.title: A stronger next Ultimate used up on a GM that is not the primary leaves the owner's badge on the sheet: only the primary tells owners
findings.where: scripts/timed-effects.mjs:147-157 (boostUltimate: any GM), 281-288 (tellOwners: primary only); scripts/call-effects.mjs:288-293 (armCall on a GM's browser), 423-446 (appendArmedCall calls boostUltimate); scripts/bridge-asks.mjs:466-477 (requestArmCall's local road)
findings.what_happens: boostUltimate runs on whichever GM's browser arms the Ultimate (appendArmedCall is 'GM-side' on any GM: a GM pressing the Ultimate on a student's sheet arms it through armCall's GM branch, or the bridge's local road). It writes the shortened list into the GMs' store there and calls tellOwners, which returns at once unless this browser is the primary. The owner's copy (timedEffectCopy) is sent only by tellOwners, an owner's ask at load or at drpgPrimaryReady, and retellTimedEffects after a restore; no watch sends it when the primary merges another GM's change. So the player's sheet keeps the 'stronger Ultimate' badge until some other row of that character is given or ended, or the page is reloaded.
findings.failure_scenario: With two GMs at the table, the second GM arms a student's Ultimate from the sheet; the second die is added and the row used up, but the student's sheet still shows the 'stronger Ultimate' badge, and the player expects it again on the next Ultimate.
findings.expected: The owner's copy follows the store on every road that changes it (the owner's standing rule of 20.11.2026: windows redraw at once when what they show changes).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a road that resends after a merge: gm-store.mjs has no per-store watch hook (grep for watch/listen/Hooks.call: only its own listener at 1732-1740); timedEffectStore's row has afterRestore only (gm-stores.mjs:1091-1096); timed-effects.mjs sends on tellOwners, the owner's asks and retell only (272-296, 313-321, 408-411). takeDespairShield and giveTimed are primary-only, so they tell; boostUltimate is the one any GM runs. Whether a second GM arming an Ultimate from the sheet is a road tables use is not measured; the sheet's Ultimate on a GM's browser goes through armCall's GM branch.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 E93-T13 (scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:100970) arms the boosted Ultimate on one GM (the primary) and reads the rows, not a player's copy. Result not read.

findings.title: A room's tier table or flat table that answers a Search with another category is not marked a substitute, so the card does not say the room gave something else
findings.where: scripts/tables-pools.mjs:893-903 (drawRoomNamed: no `substitute`), 812-821 (roomEntryAs: the find takes its own category); scripts/action-search.mjs:597 (substitute read from the draw alone); scripts/action-report.mjs:282-283
findings.what_happens: Since E14 part 2 C3 a find is granted as what it is, not as what was asked. drawRoomNamed asks the room's '<base> - Tier N' first and its flat table last, and either may hold any category: a Healing Search there can come back a knife, filed and granted as a weapon. Only drawRoomAny and drawSpare set `substitute: true`, and the card says 'the room had nothing of what you asked for' only when that flag is set. So a player who asked for something to patch them up gets a weapon with no line saying why, the case the comment at action-search.mjs:593-596 says the line exists for. tables-pools.mjs:888-890 still says a flat table 'would hand back an apple and then label it a weapon', which C3 ended.
findings.failure_scenario: A student Searches the kitchen for Healing; the GM stocked one flat 'Kitchen' table; a kitchen knife lands on their sheet as a Murder Weapon and the card says nothing about the room not having what was asked.
findings.expected: The substitute line whenever the find's category or goal is not the one asked (action-search.mjs:593-596).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a comparison of asked and found further on: action-search.mjs's outcome reads drawn.substitute alone (597); grantDrawn and traceTheFind take the drawn category without setting it. That a flat table answers every category is the owner's design (D15, tables-pools.mjs:889-891) and is not questioned; only the line is.
findings.tests_near: R1234 reads the draw's steps and order (tables-pools.mjs:972, 986-989), not the card's line. Result not read.

by_decision.what: The time of day moves in private during an incident: the card goes to the GMs and the incident's audience, veiled, and the HUD freezes for bystanders; the world setting still reaches every client.
A timed effect's end takes the bonus from whatever the sheet holds, so a trait edited back by hand reads -n after the end.
A boundary's take-back lasts five minutes and four boundaries deep: design numbers, not measured at a table.
The day boards play only on a real roll-over and Night's real start; Edit campaign, the rewind, the reset and a console's setClock take the stamps away.
A private card whose reader list comes out empty is dropped and said in the console, not posted for everybody.
whisperToOwnerOnly with no player owner goes to the acting user, so a whisper list is never empty.
An NPC of type character not in the class gets Breakdown and its bars read as a reserve.
Breakdown's and Wounded's icons are drawn on no token for anybody; the sheet says both.
A flat room table answers every category a Search asks for; the room's tables answer before the world's pools.
The Tier pools tab makes no pool and renames none; Delete stays.
Unticking a pool in Place drops every entry of that name from it.
The Event panel stands in both themes; eventsWindowActive answers true everywhere and is kept as a named predicate.
A safeword card may be posted by a player when no GM is connected, so a player's chat message with the safeword flag is a legal one.
